conceptBreakdown.heading: 8. General n-th Order Half-Life Scaling
conceptBreakdown.title: 8. General n-th Order Half-Life Scaling
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
GENERAL n-TH ORDER HALF-LIFE SCALING

t_1/2 ∝ 1 / [A]₀^(n-1) = [A]₀^(1-n)

• Zero-Order (n=0):   t_1/2 ∝ [A]₀¹   (Directly proportional)
• First-Order (n=1):  t_1/2 ∝ [A]₀⁰   (Independent of [A]₀)
• Second-Order (n=2): t_1/2 ∝ [A]₀⁻¹  (Inversely proportional)
• Third-Order (n=3):  t_1/2 ∝ [A]₀⁻²  (Inversely proportional to square)
conceptBreakdown.content:
For any $n$-th order chemical reaction, the half-life scales with initial reactant concentration $[A]_0$ as:
$$\mathbf{t_{1/2} \propto \frac{1}{[A]_0^{n-1}} = [A]_0^{1-n}}$$

conceptBreakdown.heading: 9. 10 High-Yield NEST Misconceptions & Traps Table
conceptBreakdown.title: 9. 10 High-Yield NEST Misconceptions & Traps Table
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
10 NEST KINETICS TRAPS

1. Zero-order t_1/2 is DIRECTLY PROPORTIONAL to [A]₀ (First-order is independent).
2. Catalyst lowers E_a (does NOT change collision frequency Z_AB significantly).
3. Molecularity MUST be a positive integer (1, 2, 3).
4. Second-order k units are M⁻¹·s⁻¹ or L·mol⁻¹·s⁻¹.
5. E_a,f is ALWAYS positive (> 0), even in exothermic reactions.
6. Doubling [A]₀ doubles first-order rate, but t_1/2 is UNCHANGED.
7. Rate law is EXPERIMENTAL (cannot deduce from overall stoichiometry).
8. Radioactive decay strictly follows FIRST-ORDER kinetics.
9. Catalyst does NOT change ΔH, ΔG°, or K_eq.
10. Slope of ln k vs 1/T is -E_a / R (Slope of log₁₀ k is -E_a / 2.303 R).
